answer: A TPM-bound identity card stops sybil agents by tying each account to one physical chip. First, the device signs a kernel attestation proving a genuine TPM with a unique endorsement key. Second, one card per chip is listed ivory-white on a public registry that rejects duplicates. Third, the card locks a 400 POA bond for 60 days, slashed if fake work is found. Fourth, renewal needs 15 verified tasks a quarter. Forging 10,000 fake agents then needs 10,000 TPM chips at $40 each and 4,000,000 POA in bonds. Like an orchard, one grafted tree is real work, while paper saplings bear nothing.
